chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, from his father, from Fazalah ibn Ayyub, from Umar ibn Aban, from Mansur al-Sayqal who said: I heard Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) saying:
The mutual discussion of knowledge is a study (dirasa), and study is a good prayer (salat).

key_terms.تذاكر العلم: Mutual discussion/review of knowledge — a collective intellectual practice
key_terms.دراسة: Dirasa — intensive study, repetition for comprehension and memorization
key_terms.صلاة حسنة: A good prayer — an act of worship equivalent in spiritual merit to formal salat

ai.seo_question: What does Imam al-Baqir say about discussing knowledge with others?
ai.summary: Imam al-Baqir (peace be upon him) equates the mutual discussion and review of religious knowledge with formal study, and further elevates study by comparing it to a good prayer. This teaching was directed to companions who regularly gathered to review religious knowledge, encouraging them that their scholarly exchanges were not merely intellectual exercises but acts of worship in themselves. The word 'dirasa' carries the meaning of intensive study and repetition for memorization, while 'salat' here conveys the highest form of spiritual devotion.
